concepts.title: Magnetic Field and Field Lines
concepts.definition: A magnet's influence fills the space around it as a magnetic field, mapped by field lines that run from the north pole to the south pole outside the magnet, never crossing, and crowding together where the field is strongest - as at the poles.
concepts.key_idea: Field lines are the map: direction along the line, crowding shows strength.
concepts.textbook_ref: jesc112.txt sections on magnetic field and field lines
question_patterns: what is a magnetic field - how is it detected

solution_steps.action: sprinkle the compass or iron filings
solution_steps.explain: Their alignment traces the field lines.
Direction follows the line; crowding shows strength.
Lines form closed loops from north to south outside, south to north inside.

concepts.title: Magnetic Effects of Current - Solenoid and Electromagnet
concepts.definition: Every current carries magnetism: a straight wire's field forms circles around it (right-hand thumb rule), a circular loop concentrates it at the centre, and a current-carrying solenoid behaves like a bar magnet with north and south poles - turning it into an electromagnet with a soft iron core.
concepts.key_idea: Current creates magnetism: the right-hand rule reads it, the solenoid concentrates it.
concepts.textbook_ref: jemh112 magnetic field due to current, solenoid sections
question_patterns: state the right-hand thumb rule for the field around a straight conductor

draw the field pattern of a circular current-carrying loop
list the uses of electromagnets in daily life

solution_steps.explain: Thumb along the current, fingers curl along the field.
A solenoid adds the fields of many loops into a uniform interior.
A soft iron core multiplies the field, making an electromagnet.

concepts.title: Force on a Conductor, Electric Motor and Electromagnetic Induction
concepts.definition: A current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field feels a force whose direction Fleming's left-hand rule gives - the principle of the electric motor; the reverse, moving a conductor in a field, induces current by electromagnetic induction (Fleming's right-hand rule), the principle of generators, with domestic AC supply alternating at 50 hertz.
concepts.key_idea: Motor: current plus field gives force. Generator: motion plus field gives current.
concepts.textbook_ref: jesc112.txt sections on force, motor, electromagnetic induction, domestic circuits

solution_steps.explain: Left hand for force on current, right hand for induced current.
Motors convert current to motion; generators convert motion to current.
Fuses, earthing and proper wiring keep domestic circuits safe.
